quizzes.stem: A month of support-agent sessions shows two problems: in 3 percent a refund was issued before the customer was identified, and in 9 percent the agent escalated cases that policy lets it settle. Which fix is made first?

options.a: Train a separate model on past tickets first, so it can decide which cases need a person
options.b: Write escalation criteria first, because that problem touches the larger share of sessions
options.c: Rewrite the descriptions of the tools first, since both problems start with tool choice
options.d: Enforce the call sequence in the dispatcher, because moved money cannot be recalled

explanation.d: Money that moved wrongly cannot be called back, so its cause is fixed first.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the size of a count does not set the order: "The first fix goes to what cannot be undone."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the skipped step is a step order and not a tool choice: "A step order that is only requested".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a trained model comes before words were tried: "machinery for a problem nobody has tried to fix with words".

quizzes.stem: A customer asks about a purchase that belongs to someone else. How does the support example's dispatcher refuse the call?

options.a: As `order_not_owned`, and the message does not name the owner
options.b: As `order_not_owned`, and the message names the owner of the order
options.c: As `not_found`, and the message says that the order does not exist
options.d: As `needs_human`, and the message tells the model to escalate

explanation.a: The refusal is `order_not_owned` and keeps the owner out of it: "An order that belongs to someone else is refused as `order_not_owned`, and the message does not say whose it is."
explanation.b: is ruled out by the same sentence: "the message does not say whose it is".
explanation.c: Ruled out because `not_found` is the answer of the identity step: "No match returns `not_found` with the same advice."
explanation.d: Ruled out because that refusal belongs to the amount: "above it the refusal is `needs_human`, which tells the model that the next step is to escalate".

quizzes.stem: Two customers share a name, the lookup tool returns both, and the agent proceeds with the first. What should the dispatcher have done?

options.a: Choose the customer whose order is the most recent one on file
options.b: Verify both customers, and let either be served as the case unfolds
options.c: Set nobody as verified, and have the model ask what tells them apart
options.d: Raise the retry count of the lookup until it returns one match

explanation.c: Several matches are a question for the customer, and nothing is set.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the dispatcher does not pick: "Several matches set nothing and return the refusal".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the desk holds one verified customer, set only by a single match: "One match sets the verified customer."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the refusal is not a fault that a retry can clear: "A retryable error (a timeout of the order service) is retried once by the loop, which is the loop's business, not the model's."

quizzes.stem: After a change that made the agent escalate less, first-contact resolution rose from 0.60 to 0.75 and the team reports success. What does the audit still have to show?

options.a: That tokens per conversation fell by the same proportion as the escalation rate
options.b: That sessions settled alone although a human was needed did not increase
options.c: That the prompt now holds fewer words than before the change was made
options.d: That the confidence scores of the model moved up together with the rate

explanation.b: A lower escalation rate is a success only if no case that needed a person was settled alone.
explanation.a: Ruled out because tokens are not what the change risked: "Both are visible only against labels."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the length of a prompt is not the risk: "A rate alone is a bad objective".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a number the model reports is unmeasured: "The course treats the number as a claim that has to be measured against labelled outcomes before anything is routed on it".

quizzes.stem: One session holds eleven calls to the wrong tool, and the audit reports a count of one for the wrong-tool shape. A manager asks why not eleven. What is the answer?

options.a: The audit keeps only the first mistake of each session in the report
options.b: Counts are capped at one by default, whatever the session holds
options.c: The other ten calls were retries, which the audit leaves out
options.d: The target is a share of conversations, and each fails at most once

explanation.d: The unit of the target is the conversation.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the audit does not drop later mistakes for space: "The count of steps is still a useful diagnostic for a single session."
explanation.b: Ruled out because nothing in the audit caps a count: "The audit counts each failure shape once per session."
explanation.c: Ruled out because every call was a pick of the wrong tool and none is set aside: "A conversation in which the model picked the wrong tool eleven times is one failed conversation".

quizzes.stem: The audit needs two fields for each session: whether a human was needed, and which tool each step should have used. Which source supplies them?

options.a: The tool logs, which record every call with its arguments and its result
options.b: Reviewers who label a sample of the sessions by hand
options.c: The model, which can be asked after each conversation to mark its own errors
options.d: The customer, through a short survey sent at the end of each conversation

explanation.b: A judgement about need and about the right tool is made by a person, on a sample.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the logs hold the calls and not the judgements: "Two fields are not."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the audit exists to check the agent against something other than itself: "a number computed only on what is easy to read is flattering".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a survey does not say which tool was right: "Whether a case needed a person is a judgement, and so is which tool a step should have used."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent handles returns, billing disputes and account problems with tools that verify identity, look up orders and issue refunds, and it escalates to a person when it cannot resolve a case. A worker process keeps one state object for every conversation it serves, and a customer is shown a note that belongs to someone else's order. Which change addresses the cause?

options.a: Clear the shared object once an hour, limiting how long a note stays
options.b: Create a new instance for each ticket, with nothing kept after it
options.c: Instruct the model never to repeat what another person has written
options.d: Encrypt the stored notes, with only their owner able to read them later

explanation.b: A state that belongs to one case cannot reach another.
explanation.a: Ruled out because an hourly clear still lets a note travel between cases: "so a customer's identity, the orders looked up and the refunds made cannot reach another case".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a request in a prompt is not a guarantee: "a long-lived shared state is a defect".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the fault is that one object serves every conversation, and encryption leaves it shared: "the example builds a new desk for each conversation".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent handles returns, billing disputes and account problems with tools that verify identity, look up orders and issue refunds, and it escalates to a person when it cannot resolve a case. A refund above the limit is refused, and the model asks for the same refund again, and again. What does the dispatcher need so that the run ends in a useful way?

options.a: A guard on identical calls that halts the loop and transfers to staff
options.b: A line in the prompt telling the model to stop once a refund is refused
options.c: A silent retry of the refund until the backend finally accepts it
options.d: A larger turn limit that gives the model room to find another approach

explanation.a: A guard on identical calls turns a loop into a hand-off.
explanation.d: Ruled out because more turns only prolong the loop: "the cap only ends a run, and the guard ends it with a hand-off".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a sentence of the prompt does not stop a loop: "If the same call, with the same arguments, has been made three times in a row".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a refused refund is a permanent refusal: "A permanent error is never retried."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent handles returns, billing disputes and account problems with tools that verify identity, look up orders and issue refunds, and it escalates to a person when it cannot resolve a case. An audit finds no skipped identity step and no refund over the limit, wrong tools in 14 sessions, and escalation errors in 9. Which fix comes first?

options.a: Reword the descriptions of the confusable pair, giving formats and examples
options.b: Write criteria and worked examples for when the agent should hand over a case
options.c: Add a prerequisite gate in the dispatcher in front of the order tools
options.d: Move the whole policy into a retrieval index that the agent can search

explanation.a: With nothing about money, the wrong tool in more sessions than escalation errors goes to the descriptions.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the wrong-tool count is the larger: "A wrong tool in at least as many sessions as escalation errors".
explanation.c: Ruled out because no session skipped a step and no refund went over the limit: "A protected call before a successful identity check, or a refund over the limit that was made".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the cause is in how the tools are described and not in a missing source: "the model chose by what the descriptions said".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent handles returns, billing disputes and account problems with tools that verify identity, look up orders and issue refunds, and it escalates to a person when it cannot resolve a case. A team adds a rule that hands a case to a person whenever the message holds three exclamation marks. Which audit count is likely to rise?

options.a: Sessions settled by the agent although a person was needed
options.b: Sessions with a refund made over the limit
options.c: Sessions passed upward that never required a human decision
options.d: Sessions that ran an order call before the customer was identified

explanation.c: Mood is not need, so handovers that needed no person rise.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the rule only adds handovers: "the agent resolved the case, and a person was needed".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the rule does not touch refunds: "A refund over the limit that was refused and handed to a person is not a failure."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the rule does not change the order of the calls: "A protected call before a successful identity check".
